paper_metadata.title: In Situ TiC Particle-Reinforced FeCoCrNiCu High Entropy Alloy Matrix Composites by Induction Smelting
paper_metadata.journal: Transactions of the Indian Institute of Metals

evidence.quote: In this study, in situ TiC particle-reinforced FeCoCrNiCu high entropy alloy matrix composites were prepared successfully via vacuum induction melting method.

alloy_systems.name: TiC particle-reinforced FeCoCrNiCu high-entropy alloy matrix composite

evidence.quote: The FeCoCrNiCu high entropy alloy matrix has an equiaxed grain structure, and the TiC-reinforced high entropy alloy matrix composite has a single FCC phase structure.

5 vol% TiC/FeCoCrNiCu composite material and 10 vol% TiC/FeCoCrNiCu composite

High purity of Co particles, Cr particles, Ni particles, Cu particles, Fe powders, Ti powders and C powders was used as raw materials to prepare high entropy alloy matrix, 5 vol% TiC/FeCoCrNiCu composite material and 10 vol% TiC/FeCoCrNiCu composite.

process_steps.input_state: mixed Fe, Ti and C powders

evidence.quote: To start with, a proportion of 5:1 of mixed powders (Fe, Ti and C) were ball-milled in the planetary mill (QM-ISP) for 4 h at the speed of 250 rounds/min.
Then, the mixed powders were put in a drying oven to dry for 1 h.
After pressing the powder into the cylindrical block with the oil press (FLS-50T), the mass loss was calculated and the corresponding Co, Cr, Ni, Cu particles were weighed.

other.charge: mixed Co, Cr, Ni, Cu particles with briquette

evidence.quote: The mixed particles were put into the ceramic crucible together with the briquette, and the alloy ingot was smelted in an induction heating furnace under the protective atmosphere of argon gas.

It can be seen that the main phase of FeCoCrNiCu high entropy alloy matrix composites prepared by induction melting is a simple FCC structure.
With the addition of the TiC reinforcement phase, the material still maintains the FCC structure, but the intensity of each diffraction peak chan-ges.
The composites still maintain the FCC phase structure, and the grain size increases microscopically, with Cu element segregating within the grains and on the grain boundaries.

Combined with the EDS analysis of Fig. 3b, it can be proved that the TiC-reinforced phase is generated in the composite material which is evenly distributed in the matrix. Some TiC is ﬁxed on the grain boundary, thereby enhancing the grain boundary.
It can be seen that more TiC particles are ﬁnely dispersed on the substrate, and the phenomenon of copper segregation still exists, but the degree of segregation is weakened and dispersed.
It can be seen that the alloy material has ﬁne grains, clear grain boundaries, and an equiaxed crystal state.
As shown in Fig. 3a, there is obvious segregation of the composition at the grain boundary, which is proved to be Cu by EDS detection.

While after adding 10 vol% TiC, the size of the pit becomes larger, the depth becomes shallower and obvious inclusion particles are visible, as revealed in Fig. 5b, c.

This ﬁne-grain strengthening effect not only improves the strength of the material but also increases the plasticity of the material [ 27, 28].
The thermodynamically stable and high interfacial bonding strength, can transfer load more effectively and improve the strength of the material, which is identiﬁed as load bearing effect [ 29].

When the matrix is plastically deformed, the TiC-reinforced phase acts as a pinning dislocation and hinders the dislocation. Movement causes dislocation jamming and the deformation resistance of the material increases.
Therefore, increasing the TiC volume fraction within a certain range can increase the tensile strength of the composite.
